title: Capacity Slice Priority Playbook & Adaptive Reservation Pilot — Q3 Roadmap
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary: Build a concise, repeatable playbook and pilot for 'capacity slicing' and adaptive reservation hedging that lets product teams reserve baseline capacity while enabling fast, automated bursts for variable workloads. This initiative ties into Q3 OKRs to lower tail latency incidents and reduce per-token cost by 12% for bursty customers on Dedicated plans.

Goals and success criteria: 
- Deliver a documented Capacity Slice Playbook for operators and sales engineers (playbook should include policy templates, cost tradeoffs, and rollback steps).
- Run a 6-week pilot with 3 customers representing different burst profiles (chat app, analytics embeddings pipeline, and multi-tenant PLG app).
- Validate that adaptive reservation logic reduces missed-request failures during surges by 60% and reduces billed overprovision by at least 10% across pilot participants.
- Produce dashboards in the Console showing slice utilization, hedged reservation usage, and per-customer cost delta vs baseline.

Scope: 
- Policy surface: priority-slicing rules (static baseline + ephemeral slices), hedging windows, and burst budget limits.
- Orchestration: integration with Dedicated autoscaler to allow prioritized fastpath for slices and automated fallback routes to hosted variants when slices deplete.
- Observability: new Console widgets, alerting thresholds, and per-tenant cost breakdown for slices.
- Playbook artifacts: runbook, sales-engineer onboarding checklist, customer-facing FAQ about cost/latency tradeoffs.

Out-of-scope for this Q3 slice: full billing redesign, long-term reservation marketplace, and offline/on-prem packaging changes. Those will be separate initiatives.

Stakeholders: 
- Product: Miguel (owner), Aisha (program), Jenna (capacity forecasting)
- Eng: Runtime (ENG-19812), Autoscaler (ENG-20345), Console (ENG-21098)
- Solutions & Sales Engineering: Priya, Tomas
- Customer Success: Rowan

Metrics to track: 
- Pilot: percent of surge requests served within SLO (target +60% improvement vs baseline)
- Economics: net per-customer token cost change (target -10%)
- Reliability: incidence of failover to hosted model (target <5% of surge windows)
- Adoption: number of customers added to pilot (target 3), and internal adoption score from SEs (qualitative)

Milestones and timeline (Q3 slice): 
- March: finalize policy spec and playbook draft; alignment review with Eng and Security
- April: telemetry and Console dashboard prototypes; lab testing with synthetic surge traces
- May: select pilot customers; run 6-week pilot with iterative tuning (two 3-week phases)
- June: post-pilot analysis, adjust playbook, and prepare release notes and SE enablement materials

Risks & mitigations: 
- Risk: unexpected cost backfire if slices are too conservative. Mitigation: simulate with historical traces and build guardrails (cap on hedging spend per window).
- Risk: negative latency regressions due to slice priority scheduling. Mitigation: early latency benchmarks in lab and canarying on low-risk tenants.
- Risk: API/contract confusion for customers. Mitigation: clear playbook language, FAQ, and SE scripts.

Artifacts & links: 
- Playbook draft (Confluence): https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/CAP/Capacity+Slice+Playbook
- Pilot tracker (Sheet): https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1PilotTrackerExample
- Synthetic surge traces repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/surge-traces
- Console dashboard mockups (Figma): https://www.figma.com/file/CapacitySliceMockups

Next steps (owner: Miguel): 
1) Run alignment workshop with Runtime and Autoscaler leads (target date: 2025-01-20).
2) Approve pilot customer shortlist and secure NDAs where necessary (target date: 2025-02-02).
3) Kickoff telemetry work with Console to ensure data model readiness (target date: 2025-02-16).
